newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end 97's first bourse session lower.
newsitem.headline: German shares end 97's first bourse session lower.

text.p: German equities end bourse trade well down on Thursday after the 101-point fall in the Dow Jones index on Tuesday but dealers said that the strong dollar halted any strong declines amid weak trading volumes.
By the end of the first floor session of 1997, the DAX index of 30 leading German shares stood 39.92 points, or 1.38 percent, lower at 2,848.77 points.

Earlier, the IBIS electronic share dealing system had been delayed by over an hour due to technical problems, but dealers said the lack of any serious trading volumes meant the interruption had had little impact on share values.
"The delay was of little importance because there is scarcely anybody here," one dealer said.
March DAX futures traded 41.5 points down at 2,863 points as German debt futures were also taken lower by a fall in U.S. Treasuries.
Traders said the slight recovery of the dollar to around 1.545 marks from some the low of some 1.536 marks reached on January 31, prevented German shares experiencing any further losses.

Individual share losers included banks Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank and Commerzbank which fell earlier on but these recovered somewhat over the session to end down one mark to 45.55 and 35 pfennigs to 38.75 respectively, but with volumes relatively low in both cases.
Insurer Allianz ended 54 marks lower at 2,746, while chemical and auto stocks all fell with the trend.
